verdicts.message: Array reference at (1) out of bounds (0 < 1) in loop beginning at (2)
verdicts.reason: Index X-1 (or X+1) in a loop from 1, but the first (or last) pass sits in a separate branch (IF (X.EQ.1) ... ELSE, or X.GT.1 in the condition); gfortran judges the loop without those conditions. So the reported index never falls outside the table. Apart from that, the boundary branches read index 2 and need at least two points: for SPCSIG this has been enforced since BF-25.

verdicts.message: Impure function ‘validbp’ at (1) might not be evaluated
verdicts.reason: VALIDBP returns the number of wet neighbours through WNP. WNP is only read in the THEN branch of an .AND. of which VALIDBP is an operand; that branch can only be reached if VALIDBP was executed. Where VALIDBP can be skipped, WNP is not read afterwards but set again first. Otherwise only the STRACE counter.

verdicts.message: Impure function ‘keywis_default’ at (1) might not be evaluated
verdicts.reason: Every place has the form KEYWIS('A') .OR. KEYWIS('B') with synonyms. On a match KEYWIS marks the keyword as USED; if B is skipped because A already matched, B would have given .FALSE. straight away anyway. Only the STRACE counter is lost. The one place with a different left-hand side (NSTATM.LE.0 .OR. KEYWIS('STAT')) was a real defect and has been repaired (BF-24).

verdicts.message: Same actual argument associated with INTENT(OUT) argument ‘in’ and INTENT(OUT) argument ‘out’ at (1)
verdicts.reason: In-place FFTW plan: the same scratch array as input and output is how FFTW recognises an in-place transform (FFTW manual, 'in-place'). The INTENT(OUT) on both arguments comes from FFTW's own fftw3.f03 interface. The scratch is released after planning and never read.
